title: AlphaFold-Multimer predicts cyclin-CDK substrate docking and reveals an ERL motif
summary: AlphaFold-Multimer was used to predict interactions between the fission yeast Cdc13-L-Cdc2 cyclin-CDK fusion and its known in vivo substrates. Many substrates were predicted to bind the cyclin hydrophobic patch, and a previously uncharacterised docking motif, the ERL motif, was identified. ERL motifs functionally substituted for canonical RxL motifs in promoting phosphorylation of a model CDK substrate, while the S-phase Cig2-Cdc2 preferred canonical RxL substrates. No differential binding of replication versus mitotic substrates was predicted. Yeast preprint; one model substrate tested.

evidence.tested: Phosphorylation assays with ERL versus RxL motifs on a model substrate.
evidence.unknown: Generality across substrates and organisms; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts cyclin-CDK substrate interactions and motifs.
